title: quercus pubescens subsp. lanuginosa
intro: Quercus pubescens subsp. lanuginosa, commonly known as Downy White Oak, is a subspecies of deciduous tree in the beech family, native to Eastern Europe and Western Asia. The Downy White Oak has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its various health benefits, which include lowering cholesterol levels, reducing inflammation, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Quercus pubescens subsp. lanuginosa include acting as a vasodilator, antiseptic, and anti-inflammatory agent, making it effective in treating conditions such as high blood pressure and wounds. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
